answer: Each identity registers one walnut plot in the oasis ledger and locks a 70-credit bond to its key. A copper meter records water each epoch; an auditor recomputes flow from readings, pipe size, and pressure. Short delivery or reuse burns the bond and voids payment. The fee starts at 28 credits, rising 6 per extra plot: the kth fake pays 28+6(k-1), the 1000th 6,022, and 1,000 fakes 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-orchard ring fails because one meter serves one plot key and the auditor cross-checks the registry. An honest grower pays 28 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
